mechaber/1:main: The law of two upper stories opposite one another open to a courtyard. And in it one seif: Two upper stories open to a courtyard opposite one another, and one made a depression in the courtyard in order to pour into a courtyard that lacks four amot of water, and the second did not make one; if they joined together both are permitted to pour their water; and if they did not join together and one joined for itself and the second did not join at all — the one that did not join is forbidden and the one that joined is permitted, provided she does not pour directly into the depression but pours in the upper story and they descend to the depression. {Rama: For force in an unjoined courtyard is permitted (Tur); and likewise if the courtyard is more than four amot both are permitted in this manner and need no depression (Beit Yosef).}
baer-heitev/1:_: She made a depression. See what is written there at length — Taz.
beer-hagolah/1:ד: (ד) And details of the law of a depression are explained siman 327).
beur-hagra/1:א: (א) Seif 1. And one joined, etc. until permitted. Tur's wording — doubt; and in siman 372 it is a textual error — it should read: and one for itself and the second did not make — the one that did not make, etc.
beur-hagra/1:ב: (ב) For force in a courtyard. Tosafos there; and specifically in a courtyard, but in karmelis they decreed as written chapter 9a s.v. "they did not teach"; and Shabbat 100b s.v. "force"; and above siman 357 seif 3 in the gloss.
beur-hagra/1:ג: (ג) And the same law if. Mishnah there chapter 8a — as above.
biur-halacha/1:א: And one made a depression, etc. — Beit Yosef brought Tosafos' explanation on this passage; Rambam also has another explanation of this mishnah in commentary on the mishnah and likewise in his laws; but per Tosafos' explanation Rashba and Ritva also wrote, and they wrote that most commentators wrote thus.
biur-halacha/1:ב: And one joined for itself and the second did not join — per the Mechaber's initial depiction that one did not make a depression, this law applies even when both joined each for itself: the one that made a depression is permitted and the one that did not is forbidden [later authorities].
biur-halacha/1:ג: (ג) More than four amot — not precise; likewise even four amot, as above siman 357.
biur-halacha/1:ד: And they need no depression — see Mishna Berurah; Taz questions Beit Yosef — his view: since there is a depression in the courtyard we fear one will carry utensils with wastewater there; he brought proof from Rambam and many later authorities rejected his proof [Tosafos Yeshanim, Nehar Shalom, Avkat Rochel, Atzei Almogim — Rambam refers only to the first part of Rambam's words, not the latter]; nevertheless many rishonim wrote like Rashi — it deals with a courtyard less than four amot — Rashba, Ritva, Or Zarua; see Atzei Almogim — likewise in rainy season no depression needed, as siman 357 even under four amot both are permitted.
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (א) And one made a depression, etc. — adjacent below opposite her upper story.
mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (ב) In order to pour into a courtyard that lacks, etc. — in such a courtyard forbidden to pour water without a depression for it, as siman 357 seif 1; see there. If the courtyard has four amot — see end of seif in gloss and what we wrote there.
mishnah-berurah/1:ג: (ג) To pour their water — even directly into the depression.
mishnah-berurah/1:ד: (ד) And one joined, etc. — the one that made the depression with all neighbors dwelling at her upper story; deals when each upper story has a balcony before it, all enter the balcony via the upper story opening, and from it descend to the courtyard.
mishnah-berurah/1:ה: (ה) Forbidden — even if she too made a depression [and all the more so per the Mechaber when she did not make a depression]; not only forbidden to carry utensils with wastewater through the courtyard to her depression or to the balcony since she joined only for the upper story — even to pour in her house so water goes by itself to the balcony and descends — forbidden, lest he spare spoilage of his house from wastewater and carry utensils with wastewater directly to the shared balcony, since he did not join with other upper story residents.
mishnah-berurah/1:ו: (ו) And she who joined is permitted — provided she made a depression as above; without a depression forbidden to pour in her house or to a balcony lest water descend to the courtyard and certainly to reshus ha-rabbim as siman 357; even if her neighbor made a depression and water would descend from the courtyard to that depression — forbidden, lest he fear courtyard spoilage since the depression is far and he carries house utensils to the courtyard to pour directly into the depression — they did not join together.
mishnah-berurah/1:ז: (ז) That she not pour directly into the depression — for the courtyard is shared by both and they did not join together.
mishnah-berurah/1:ח: (ח) As in an unjoined courtyard, etc. — meaning: even though the courtyard with the depression belongs to both and water descends there to the depression by his force.
mishnah-berurah/1:ט: (ט) Both are permitted, etc. — meaning permitted to pour also onto the balcony and descend to the courtyard; deals when each joined for itself; we do not fear he will carry utensils with water to the courtyard to pour into the depression his neighbor made, since the courtyard has four amot of such width that water is absorbed in place and the courtyard is not ruined.
mishnah-berurah/1:י: (י) And need no depression — meaning therefore even if one made a depression on his upper story side we do not fear the second will carry utensils with wastewater there.
magen-avraham/1:א: (א) That did not join — forbidden. Even if she made a depression — forbidden to carry onto the balcony; thus even to pour in her house forbidden — we fear she will spare house spoilage and carry utensils to the balcony.
magen-avraham/1:ב: (ב) Permitted. Provided she made a depression; but forbidden to pour on the balcony lest water descend from courtyard to the depression her neighbor made — we fear she will fear courtyard spoilage since the depression is far and bring house utensils to the courtyard to pour near the depression — so Bach; in briefs it does not imply thus — see there; and it appears to me he wrote "the second did not join at all" — if the second joined for itself it does not forbid the courtyard and the one that made a depression may pour directly into the depression; but whoever did not join at all has forbidden foot in its place and forbids the courtyard — Eruvin 98 and doubt; see siman 364 seif 3.
machatzit-hashekel/1:_: (Siman 1) Even if she made, etc. — Bach questioned: why teach "did not join for itself" — even if she joined for itself, forbidden to pour on the balcony lest water descend to neighbor's depression — as in the Talmud: since neighbor's depression is far from her balcony she fears if water descends from balcony to courtyard then to depression the whole courtyard will be muddied — therefore she lowers utensils with water to the courtyard to pour into the depression — forbidden since they did not join together; therefore Bach wrote why teach "did not join for itself" — to forbid in every case even if she too made a depression — forbidden to carry onto the balcony since upper story residents did not join with one another.
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: (a) And the second did not join at all, etc. — if the second joined for itself it does not forbid the courtyard and the one that joined may pour directly into the depression; but when she did not join at all it is forbidden foot in its place and forbids the courtyard — see beginning siman 372 (Magen Avraham).
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (1) [Seif 1] And one made a depression in the courtyard, etc. — already explained Rashi siman 357: a courtyard adjacent to reshus ha-rabbim lacking four amot fit to absorb se'ah of water a person needs daily — then need a depression in the courtyard for water to descend; then even if they go outside he is not pleased thus and it is not direct pouring to reshus ha-rabbim as written there; therefore if one made a depression and they joined together both are permitted. Tosafos Yeshanim Orach:
turei-zahav/1:_: She made a depression in the courtyard, etc. In this seif Tur's wording was brought; I greatly struggled to settle this and could not — in the mishnah: two dyot opposite one another, part made a depression and part did not — the one that made is permitted and the one that did not is forbidden; Rava said: only when they did not join; but if they joined, permitted; and if they did not join why forbidden? Rav Ashi said: a decree lest they bring utensils from houses there; Tosafos questioned: if they did not join, both should be forbidden; answer: they do not pour directly into the depression in the courtyard but pour onto the dyot and water descends to the adjacent depression; even though the courtyard is unjoined, sages did not forbid here, etc.; those who did not make a depression are forbidden lest they bring water in house utensils here because they do not want water to fall and ruin the courtyard — a fine distinction between the upper story that made the depression and the opposite one without: the other, being far from the depression, will not pour from the upper story lest water flow to the depression and ruin the courtyard — unlike the one that made the depression adjacent to it who need not pour to the courtyard at all. Tur follows Tosafos and added words without context — in the case they did not join he distinguished upper stories regarding joining for themselves — if one joined for itself and the second did not join at all — what eruv is needed here? Since there is no courtyard eruv together, what eruv does the upper story make for itself without the courtyard? Who requested this? What did he fix? No hint in Gemara and poskim; Tur's own wording is mixed — he began with making the depression forbidding the other for lack of depression, ended with prohibition for not joining for itself; if it needs separate eruv and did not join — what of the depression? Mahariv tried to explain there is a balcony — readers find no answer; he concluded many err with strange explanations; I have seen no explanation; perhaps textual error or omission in Tur; wonder that Beit Yosef did not notice and brought it in Shulchan Aruch — leave it to one with calm heart. Levush was asked and answered: reason from depression near one and far from other is untrue — it depends only on depression and eruv as Tosafos — main distinction between upper stories besides no explanation for "and likewise if residents of the second," etc. — why doesn't one's depression help the other? He wrote without precision forgivingly; Mechaber there properly raises difficulty and he does not answer. Beit Yosef wrote: deals with courtyard less than four amot — if more, do not pour directly unless joined; if not joined each pours in its domain and water goes by force to unjoined courtyard — we do not fear carrying utensils since courtyard measure exists — end; Rabbi thought fear only in small courtyard — wonder: with depression adjacent to other upper story why ruin small courtyard — water flows to depression; what is different in large courtyard — same fear; certainly one fear in large courtyard without joint eruv with depression near one upper story — far one will not pour lest soil be dirtied and lower house utensils — applies also to four amot with depression; Rashi on mishnah: courtyard before them less than four amot because depression law applies to such courtyard; Beit Yosef and Rama: if four amot they do not regularly pour into depression on weekdays but sometimes to courtyard itself — on Shabbat no fear if pouring on upper story descending to ground — Rambam wrote this law chapter 4; Maggid Mishneh: deals with courtyard four by four — doubt.
peri-megadim/1:א: (א) She made — in siman 372 Bach and Magen Avraham letter 1 — will be explained. Mechaber brought Tur here and omitted Rambam chapter 4 Eruvin 27 as he usually brings: two dyot, etc. — do not pour until they join; one made depression and two did not — those who poured to depression and two did not until they join; both made depression each pours to depression even without joining. Three divisions and two middle divisions and beginning — like Tosafos Eruvin 89a and as unjoined courtyard chapter 33 as Taz here; but beginning division implies both did not make depression — therefore courtyard with four amot deals as Maggid Mishneh — otherwise in less than four amot possible without depression as chapter 15 and siman 357 seif 1; deals pouring directly to courtyard not via dyot then to courtyard — why this division? In less than four with depression should teach forbidden to pour directly to depression without joint eruv as direct to unjoined courtyard via dyot to depression — two divisions. Rather two aspects: first like beginning — courtyard with four amot — necessarily two other divisions; all where one made depression and two did not without joint eruv — second forbidden since we see they care about courtyard cleanliness by making depression — fear second will bring wastewater to courtyard below to depression — not absolute necessity — for Rambam when courtyard open to karmelis force in karmelis chapter 33a; default deals with open to reshus ha-rabbim Eruvin 98. From Maggid Mishneh chapter 15 and not here "one made depression" — implies latter part also more than four amot — all where one made depression cares about cleanliness — second forbidden. Second aspect: neither made depression even in more than four amot both forbidden even to pour on dyot then to courtyard since most people are particular not to dirty courtyard center — even more than four amot permitted without depression siman 357 — they usually pour at courtyard sides; if both joined neither made depression — one made and two did not forbidden even to dyot then courtyard fearing they will descend with wastewater and spill at courtyard sides under dyot and carry in courtyard without eruv. Beit Yosef and Rabbenu Yerucham imply Rambam beginning: pouring directly into it — courtyard — feminine — Rambam: two dyot opposite with one courtyard beneath — pouring into it means courtyard — do not pour without eruv directly — to dyot then courtyard permitted; middle and end where one made depression even in more than four forbidden — we see cleanliness concern — fear second will lower — first explanation; Rabbenu Yerucham ends: need no depression; Taz questioned should state specifically when neither made depression — understand; Tosafos Yeshanim wondered on Taz; Avkat Rochel: Rambam refers to beginning as I wrote.
peri-megadim/1:ב: (ב) And what is written — Eruvin 11a s.v. "and that he wrote" fear for dyot spoilage — apparently error — should be courtyard spoilage lacking four amot — if dyot spoilage both should be forbidden — doubt; and with God's help Magen Avraham will explain further Pri Megadim and Levush briefly — not to expand here.
netiv-chayim/1:_: (Magen Avraham siman 1) And it appears to me he wrote "the second," etc. — doubt; still difficult: even with depression both forbidden — cannot go with water to upper dyot since they did not join for themselves; want to establish his words because they did not make depression — even to pour in house forbidden for house spoilage — unknown what this fixes; why teach lack of depression — even with depression; Taz wondered — see there; God enlightened me to reconcile Tur: those who made depression joined for themselves — "permitted" implies all permitted — water only via dyot as Tosafos and Rosh; if not joined for themselves lower ones forbidden to carry water via upper dyot; those without depression all forbidden for lack of depression; deals with no join at all for themselves — if joined, permitted foot in place permits house utensils in courtyard — cannot ask: even if made depression; if made depression not concerned for courtyard spoilage — upper resident permitted via dyot — why teach all forbidden — therefore "did not make depression" — then even upper forbidden for courtyard spoilage carrying house utensils — understand.
yad-ephraim/1:_: In Taz siman 1: it is such a courtyard. Note: as siman 357 — in courtyard of four amot no depression needed — see there.
